title: The 'if X were the main building' readings ignore the count typed, yet the Stories row offers 'Enter the number of stories', and entering a count changes nothing
detail: _stories_over now passes stated=None for as_main candidates. With the starting house assumed (main not picked), a plain building of 14 ft or more read as the main one gives readings 1..floor(h/7) and the question 'draw its floors or enter the count'. stories_needed() matches 'enter the count', so present.py adds 'stories' to needs and the row shows 'Enter the number of stories'. Entering any count leaves that candidate unchanged, so the row stays in review with the same text. refused_stories returns None, so the architect gets no message and is stuck in a loop. The present.py override (bound.split('; ')[-1]) then shows only the LAST question: MAIN_QUESTION ('Which building is the main building …'). The 'could hold' question that drew the button is hidden, and so is the accessory question. That question also calls the other solid '(the building)', because len(parts)==1 for an as_main candidate, so it names the wrong object. Repro (test_present helpers, 106 lot, no main picked, no stories): three floor blocks f0..f2 plus box(40,66,50,86,0,20,'garage'). Result: ('needs_review', 'Which building is the main building … (main_building).', ['stories'], '1 to 3'). After update_counts(base, {'stories': 3}) the result is identical.
evidence: measure.py:857 `r = _stories_whole(parts, g, why_g, None if c["kind"] == "as_main" else stated)`; present.py:852-854 `["stories"] if ... rhino_logic.stories_needed(measured.get("stories"))`; present.py:804-807 `q = bound.split("; ")[-1].replace(" (story)", "")`; measure.py:701 `name = "the building" if len(parts) == 1 else tallest["id"]`.
suggested_fix: Offer the Enter button only when a typed count can settle the question: only when the question comes from a candidate that reads the count, not from an as_main candidate. Otherwise point to 'Pick the main building…'. In present.py, pick the segment that holds 'could hold up to' rather than the last '; ' segment, and keep the other open questions. For an as_main candidate, name the solid by its id.
pin: test_present: three floor blocks plus a plain 20 ft garage, main not picked, no stories. Assert either that 'stories' is not in Stories.needs, or that entering 3 changes the row. Assert the reason names the garage, not '(the building)'. It must fail on 22cdce0.
skeptics:
I could not refute this. I read the code and ran the repro, and the finding holds.

Code read:
- measure.py:857 passes `None if c["kind"] == "as_main" else stated` to _stories_whole, so a count the architect types never reaches an as_main candidate.
- measure.py:695-722 is the plain-part branch. It builds the 'could hold up to N' text, and the name on measure.py:701 is 'the building' when len(parts)==1. With nothing typed it returns the at-least/at-most readings, and the question asks the architect to 'draw its floors or enter the count'.
- _stories_over (measure.py:860-875) joins the two candidates' questions, then adds ACCESSORY and MAIN_QUESTION.
- rhino_logic.py:140-145: stories_needed looks for the words 'enter the count'. present.py:852-854 then adds 'stories' to needs, which shows the row's Enter button.
- present.py:804-807 keeps only the last '; ' piece of the question, which is MAIN_QUESTION.
- rhino_logic.py:148-153: refused_stories returns None here, because the reason has no 'fewer than'/'more than' wording.

Repro: I used the test_present helpers with the venv python on the 106 lot, no main building picked and no stories set, with floor blocks f0..f2 plus box(40,66,50,86,0,20,'garage'). It printed `needs_review | Which building is the main building (the starting house is assumed, not picked) is a question (main_building). | ['stories'] | 1 to 3 | None`. After update_counts(base, {'stories': 3}) the output was exactly the same. So the Enter button is offered, entering a count changes nothing, and no message explains why.

This is not a pre-existing issue. The diff from 904e6d7 to 22cdce0 adds the 'could hold up to' range logic in measure.py and adds both the stories_needed needs entry and the 'could hold' reason override in present.py.

Mitigating factor: picking the main building would clear the as_main candidate, so the architect has a way out. The defect is still real, because the row offers an input that has no effect.

The repro was a throwaway test that used the test_present/test_measure helpers: the 106 lot from _sample106, the main building not picked, no stories typed, three floor blocks f0..f2 and box(40,66,50,86,0,20,'garage'). The Stories row came back as ('needs_review', 'Which building is the main building (the starting house is assumed, not picked) is a question (main_building).', ['stories'], '1 to 3'), and logic.enter_words(needs) gave 'Enter the number of stories'. - measure.py:701-723 (the _stories_whole plain path) then always asks 'draw its floors or enter the count' for a 20 ft garage, which could hold 1 to 2 stories. Line 702 names it 'the building' because it is the only part.

title: The Stories range override wipes the worst-case words 'At worst 4 against 3: does not comply under that reading'
detail: The block just above sets why = 'At worst {worst} against {limit}: does not comply under that reading. …' so the bad reading is said first (architect review). The new block then replaces why with the 'could hold up to' sentence alone. For a plain 30 ft house in R-1b (3 allowed), the row no longer says that the top of the range (4) breaks the limit. It only says 'A 30 ft solid (the building) could hold up to 4 stories: draw its floors or enter the count.' The test pins that exact string.
evidence: present.py:797-800 `why = (f"At worst {worst[0]} against {worst[1]}: does not comply under that reading. " + (why or ""))` then 805-807 `why = q[0].upper() + q[1:] + "."` (overwrites); test_present.py:1225 asserts the bare sentence.
suggested_fix: Prepend or append the 'could hold' sentence to the existing why instead of replacing it, e.g. 'At worst 4 against 3: does not comply under that reading. A 30 ft solid … enter the count.'
pin: test_present test_the_stories_row_asks_for_the_whole_buildings_count_and_takes_it: for the 30 ft plain house, assert 'At worst 4' in reason and 'could hold up to 4' in reason.

The comment there says "say the bad one first: 'probably fine' it isn't", which is the architect-review rule. Then present.py:804-807, new in 904e6d7...22cdce0, assigns `why = q[0].upper() + q[1:] + "."` without adding anything to it, so the earlier text is thrown away.

title: A main building under 7 ft refuses every typed count, but its row still offers 'Enter the number of stories', so it loops
detail: `if most == 0: return _missing("stories", stop("no_stories"))` runs before the stated count is looked at. At the base commit, one plain part with a count typed took that count. Now box(…,0,6) with stories 1 still gives no_stories. Its text includes 'enter the number of stories', so stories_needed adds the Enter button. Entering 1 gives the same reason, and refused_stories says nothing (it doesn't match no_stories). Every building has at least a first story (§325-3: from a floor level to the roof), so least should be 1 for the main part.
evidence: Probe: `C 6ft entered1 ('needs_review', "no floor blocks are drawn … or enter the number of stories", ['stories'], '—') None`.
suggested_fix: Give the main part a least of 1 whatever its height, or check the stated count before the most==0 stop. If the no_stories stop stays, don't offer a button that can't resolve it.
pin: test_measure: measure(site(RECT, box(10,25,35,65,0,6)), {**FACTS, 'stories': 1})['stories']['value'] == 1, or (if refused) a refusal message that refused_stories returns.
skeptics:

For a single plain solid under 7 ft, could = 0, so most = 0 and `least` = 0. The `if most == 0: return _missing("stories", stop("no_stories"))` check then returns before the `if stated is not None` block (lines 706-716) runs. So any typed count is ignored.

At the base commit, `len(parts) == 1` with a count typed recorded that count ("stated by the architect"). That makes this a regression introduced by this diff, not an old problem.

title: A count of 0 on a plain building is refused as 'fewer than the floor blocks drawn (1)' when no floor blocks are drawn
detail: update_counts accepts 0. When counted is None, least is 1 (one story), and stated < least reuses stories_below_floors with drawn=least. The architect is told about floor blocks that don't exist.
evidence: measure.py:704-705 `if stated < least: return _missing("stories", stop("stories_below_floors", typed=f"{stated:g}", drawn=least))`; rhino_logic.update_counts allows `n >= 0`.
suggested_fix: Use a separate stop when counted is None ('a building has at least one story'), or keep stories_below_floors only when counted is set.
pin: test_measure: a plain 30 ft box with stories 0. Assert the reason does not contain 'floor blocks drawn'.

title: Duplicate 'parts_overlap' key in the STOPS dict literal
detail: The edit that removed stories_below_blocks pasted a second copy of the parts_overlap entry. Python keeps the second one silently. The values are identical today, but editing one copy has no effect if the other is the later one, and linters flag it.
evidence: stops.py:70 and :72 both `"parts_overlap": "part of the building ({what}) starts partly inside the one below it ...`
pin: A test that parses stops.py with ast and asserts no duplicate keys in the STOPS dict.
skeptics: The finding is real. I read packages/model_measurement/model_measurement/stops.py at HEAD 22cdce0. Lines 70-71 and 72-73 are two identical `"parts_overlap": "part of the building ({what}) starts partly inside the one below it (from {low} ft to {high} ft): move it to stand on the one below, or join them"` entries in the same dict literal. Running grep for `"parts_overlap"` finds two matches at 22cdce0 (lines 70 and 72) and only one on the base 904e6d7 (line 72). So this branch added the duplicate; it was not there before. Python keeps the last value without any warning. Because both strings are identical today, nothing behaves differently at runtime. The cost is maintenance: an edit to the first copy at line 70 would do nothing, and linters flag duplicate keys (pyflakes F601). P3 / DRY is the right rating.

The finding holds, and this branch introduced it. I read `stops.py` at 22cdce0, which is also the working tree. The `STOPS` dict literal has two `"parts_overlap"` keys, at line 70 and line 72, and their strings are identical. At 904e6d7 the file has one `parts_overlap` key (line 72). The diff confirms it. The change that took out `stories_below_blocks` put back a second copy of the `parts_overlap` entry as a `+` line, right below the existing one. Python silently keeps the later copy. Since both say the same thing, nothing behaves differently today. The cost is the one the finding names: a later edit to line 70 would do nothing, and linters such as pyflakes (F601) flag repeated keys. It is a real issue, but only P3.

title: The _stories_whole docstring still describes the old rule (a plain part is never counted from its height)

A part that isn't floor blocks … is never counted from its height or its blocks: the count typed stands … only if it is at least … the solids stacked in any plain part'. The new code reads a plain part's stories from its height (floor(h/7)) and has dropped the stacked-solids check.
suggested_fix: Rewrite the docstring to the new rule: least/most from the drawing, the count accepted only within [least, most], and the as_main candidates ignoring the count.
